Simulate trials with a prespecified endpoint-horizon schedule

Source: R/sim_horizon_trials.R
sim_horizon_trials.Rd

Simulates only reached interim looks under a prespecified schedule, using separate success and futility prediction data cuts. Use sim_horizon_paths() when comparing many schedules or stopping thresholds.

Usage

sim_horizon_trials(
  hazard_treatment,
  hazard_control = NULL,
  cutpoints = NULL,
  N_total,
  lambda = 0.3,
  lambda_time = NULL,
  endpoint_schedule,
  final_horizon,
  dropout_horizon = final_horizon,
  horizon_settings = NULL,
  prior_surv = c(0.1, 0.1),
  prior_bin = c(1, 1),
  bin_method = "mc",
  block = 2,
  rand_ratio = c(control = 1, treatment = 1),
  prop_loss = 0,
  alternative = "greater",
  h0 = 0,
  N_impute = 500,
  N_mcmc = 1000,
  mc_conf_level = 0.95,
  N_trials = 10,
  method = "logrank",
  imputed_final = FALSE,
  empty_interval = c("prior", "propagate", "error"),
  ncores = 1L,
  backend = c("auto", "fork", "psock", "sequential"),
  seed = NULL,
  prior_surv_final = prior_surv,
  generation_cutpoints = cutpoints,
  Fn = 0.05,
  Sn = 0.9,
  Qn = 1,
  prob_ha = 0.95,
  return_trace = FALSE
)

Arguments

hazard_treatment

A required numeric vector of finite, non-negative event rates for the treatment arm. Supply one rate per interval defined by generation_cutpoints; a single value specifies a constant event rate.

hazard_control

NULL (the default) for a single-arm trial, or a numeric vector of finite, non-negative event rates for the control arm in a two-arm trial. It must contain one rate per interval defined by generation_cutpoints.

cutpoints

Master piecewise-exponential analysis cutpoints, strictly inside final_horizon. Each endpoint uses only cutpoints strictly before that endpoint and the corresponding leading intervals of prior_surv and prior_surv_final. If an endpoint H lies inside a master interval, the same hazard parameter and unscaled Gamma prior apply, but its success update uses events and exposure only through H. Available observations beyond H are excluded even within that interval; H is not a new hazard-change assumption in the generating model.

N_total

A required positive integer giving the maximum total sample size.

lambda

A numeric vector of finite, positive enrollment rates per unit of calendar time. Supply one rate for each interval defined by lambda_time. The default is 0.3. See enrollment() for the continuous-time enrollment model and time origin.

lambda_time

NULL (the default), or a numeric vector of finite, positive, strictly increasing calendar times at which the enrollment rate changes. Time zero is implicit, and length(lambda) must equal length(lambda_time) + 1.

endpoint_schedule

Data frame with exactly two numeric columns, N and horizon, containing every planned interim enrollment size in increasing order and a positive, nondecreasing endpoint horizon at each look. All interim sizes must be less than N_total. The saved horizons are derived as sort(unique(c(endpoint_schedule$horizon, final_horizon))) and evaluated at every look, allowing subsequent comparison of schedules using the same looks and endpoint times. Use a zero-row data frame with numeric columns when there are no interims.

final_horizon

Required endpoint time for the maximum-\(N\) final analysis, all futility predictions, and planned outcome collection for every participant from enrollment. It must be at least every scheduled horizon. The generating hazards must describe this entire period.

dropout_horizon

Reference time at which prop_loss specifies the independent exponential dropout probability. Defaults to final_horizon; it remains fixed when the analysis endpoint changes.

horizon_settings

Optional data frame with one row per distinct scheduled horizon plus final_horizon, identified by column horizon. Optional columns are h0, rmst_tau, and a list column prior_bin. Missing columns use the common h0, the endpoint horizon itself for RMST restriction, and the common prior_bin, respectively. These settings are fixed within a set of trial paths.

prior_surv

A numeric vector, matrix, or named list specifying the Gamma prior for the piecewise-exponential hazards used to generate outcomes during interim prediction. A length-two vector supplies shape and rate and applies the same prior to every arm and interval. A 2 by length(cutpoints) + 1 matrix supplies interval-specific values shared by all arms, with shapes in row 1 and rates in row 2. For independent arm-specific priors, supply a list named control and treatment in a two-arm design, or treatment in a single-arm design. Each list element may be a length-two vector or an interval-specific matrix. Both arms must be supplied; no values are borrowed or filled from the other arm. Rates must use the same time unit as event times, exposure, and cutpoints. The default is c(0.1, 0.1).

prior_bin

A length-two numeric vector of finite, positive shape parameters c(a, b) for the Beta(a, b) event-probability prior used when method = "bayes-bin". The same prior is applied to both arms. The default is c(1, 1), a uniform prior.

bin_method

A single character string selecting how to calculate the posterior probability for method = "bayes-bin". It must be one of "mc" (Monte Carlo sampling), "normal" (normal approximation), or "quadrature" (numerical integration). The default is "mc". The normal approximation can be inaccurate with sparse events or non-events and posterior event probabilities near 0 or 1. It can change whether prob_ha is exceeded. Increasing N_mcmc does not improve this approximation; use "quadrature" or sufficiently precise "mc" instead. In two-arm designs, quadrature can also return an inaccurate posterior probability without an error when the posterior event risks are tightly concentrated, particularly with many participants but very few events or non-events. Check such probabilities against sufficiently precise Monte Carlo Beta draws ("mc"). Increasing N_mcmc does not improve quadrature. This integration issue does not apply to the single-arm Beta CDF calculation. Symmetry and posterior mean-variance checks issue one combined warning per simulation run if they detect an inaccurate two-arm quadrature probability, using an absolute tolerance of 1e-6. Affected results retain a quadrature_diagnostics attribute with counts of flagged calculations. The checks do not change probabilities, stopping decisions, or trial inclusion; absence of a warning does not establish numerical accuracy.

block

A positive integer vector of permitted randomization block sizes. Every value must be a multiple of sum(rand_ratio). The default is 2 and the argument is ignored for a single-arm trial.

rand_ratio

A length-two positive integer vector giving the control to treatment randomization ratio. The default is c(control = 1, treatment = 1). Name the values control and treatment; either supplied order is accepted and matched by name. A legacy unnamed vector remains accepted in c(control, treatment) order. Unequal unnamed values produce a warning because names may be required in a future major release. See randomization() for more details.

prop_loss

Dropout probability by dropout_horizon, with the same arm-specific conventions as sim_trial_data(). The corresponding dropout hazard is held fixed across all endpoint horizons.

alternative

A single character string specifying the alternative hypothesis. It must be one of "greater" (the default), "less", or "two.sided". One-sided alternatives ("greater" and "less") are supported for method = "bayes-surv" and method = "bayes-bin". All three options are supported for method = "logrank", method = "cox", method = "rmst", method = "riskdiff-wald", and method = "riskdiff-fm". For an adverse event, benefit is in the "greater" direction for RMST (longer event-free time) and the "less" direction for the other methods (lower hazard or event probability).

h0

Common null value or margin, overridden by horizon_settings$h0 when supplied. Bayesian and risk-difference methods use event-probability scales, Cox uses log hazard ratio, RMST uses treatment-control differences in time units, and log-rank requires zero. See sim_trials() for method-specific directions and allowable ranges.

N_impute

A positive integer giving the number of predictive imputations used at each interim look and, when requested, for final multiple imputation. The default is 500. An imputed Cox, RMST, or risk-difference final analysis requires at least two. For method = "bayes-surv" with empty_interval = "prior", this controls interim prediction only; the final analysis uses N_mcmc posterior draws.

N_mcmc

A positive integer giving the number of posterior draws used for Bayesian survival analyses and Bayesian binomial analyses with bin_method = "mc". The default is 1000. Ignored for all other analyses, including bin_method = "normal" and "quadrature" with method = "bayes-bin"; NULL is allowed when ignored. For the final application of method = "bayes-surv" with empty_interval = "prior", use substantially more than the default: 50000 draws is a starting point, with a larger prespecified budget (for example, 500000) near the success threshold. Assess Monte Carlo uncertainty relative to prob_ha; no fixed count guarantees a stable decision arbitrarily close to the threshold. These are independent Gamma posterior draws, despite the argument name. This setting also controls posterior draws within interim predictions, so increasing it increases interim computation; there is no separate final-only draw argument. Small counts in examples are illustrative, and operating characteristics should be assessed using the intended analysis settings.

mc_conf_level

A single numeric probability strictly between 0.5 and 1, giving the confidence level for one-sided exact binomial bounds reported as diagnostics of finite Monte Carlo uncertainty. The bounds do not alter completed-data success classifications or interim decisions, which use strict point-estimate comparisons with prob_ha, Qn, Sn, and Fn. The default is 0.95.

N_trials

A positive integer giving the number of independent trials to simulate. The default is 10.

method

A single character string specifying the completed-data and final analysis. Available choices are a log-rank (method = "logrank") test, Cox proportional hazards regression model Wald test (method = "cox"), a restricted mean survival time difference Wald test (method = "rmst"), a fully-Bayesian piecewise-exponential analysis (method = "bayes-surv"), a Bayesian beta-binomial analysis of complete binary outcomes (method = "bayes-bin"), a frequentist risk-difference Wald test (method = "riskdiff-wald"), or a Farrington-Manning score test (method = "riskdiff-fm") of complete binary outcomes. The deprecated method = "riskdiff" is accepted as an alias for "riskdiff-wald" with a warning. The default is "logrank". See Details.

imputed_final

Logical; whether to impute outcomes lost before the selected endpoint in final analyses. Defaults to FALSE. For method = "bayes-surv" with empty_interval = "prior", both values use the observed-data posterior at the selected endpoint, retaining censored follow-up; averaging completed-data posteriors under the same model and prior targets this posterior directly. Final precision is controlled by N_mcmc, while N_impute controls interim prediction. Other final-imputation methods and restrictions are the same as in sim_trials(): log-rank imputation is unavailable, and Farrington-Manning imputation requires no missing outcomes. Cox, RMST, and risk-difference Wald imputation require at least two imputations and positive pooled variance.

empty_interval

A single character string specifying how to handle empty piecewise-exponential intervals when updating Gamma hazard models for predictive imputation and Bayesian survival analysis. An empty interval is an interval with no exposed subjects in a treatment arm at the analysis time. "prior" (the default) leaves the interval at zero exposure time and zero events, so its posterior is driven only by its assigned survival prior. "propagate" is a legacy heuristic that copies exposure time and event counts from the nearest non-empty interval in the same treatment arm and emits a warning. "error" stops when any empty interval is found.

ncores

A positive integer giving the maximum number of processor cores to use. The default is 1L, which runs trials sequentially. The number actually used cannot exceed N_trials; with backend = "auto", at least two trials are required per core to justify the parallel-processing overhead.

backend

A single character string selecting the computational method. "auto" (the default) runs sequentially when ncores = 1 or fewer than four trials are requested; otherwise it uses fork-based parallelization on Unix-like systems and a PSOCK cluster on Windows. "fork", "psock", and "sequential" select a method explicitly. Forking is unavailable on Windows.

seed

NULL (the default), or a single integer between 0 and .Machine$integer.max. A supplied seed gives reproducible simulations, including when trials are run in parallel, and leaves the pre-existing random-number state unchanged.

prior_surv_final

Gamma prior for final-stage imputation and Bayesian survival analysis of completed predictive and final data. Accepts the same master-grid forms as prior_surv and defaults to it. At each endpoint, only the corresponding leading intervals are used. Supply both priors explicitly to separate predictive and analysis assumptions.

generation_cutpoints

NULL, or a numeric vector of finite, positive, strictly increasing interior follow-up times defining the piecewise-exponential model used to generate event times. hazard_treatment and hazard_control must each have one value per resulting interval. Defaults to cutpoints, preserving the historical behavior in which generation and analysis used one partition.

Fn

Futility threshold: one probability repeated at every interim or one per scheduled look. NULL or zero disables futility; the default is 0.05.

Sn

Expected-success threshold: one probability repeated at every interim or one per scheduled look. The default is 0.9; one disables expected-success stopping.

Qn

Immediate-success threshold: one probability repeated at every interim or one per scheduled look. It must be at least Sn at every look. The default, one, disables immediate-success stopping.

prob_ha

A single numeric probability in [0, 1] defining success in each completed-data analysis. For Bayesian methods this is compared with the posterior probability of the alternative; for frequentist methods it is compared with 1 - P. The default is 0.95.

return_trace

Logical; whether to include a traces data frame containing the reached interim decisions in the returned list. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A simulation result as described in apply_horizon_rules(). The calculation_failures component additionally records failed simulation stages. The complete trial paths are not retained.

Details

At a 12-month look with an eventual 18-month final endpoint, success imputation is fitted only to available data through month 12; futility imputation is fitted to available data through month 18. Both respect the look's calendar date. The schedule changes only if the trial reaches the corresponding look. It is not selected using interim outcomes.

Later interim calculations are skipped after a stop. The selected cohort's final analysis and the maximum-\(N\) final analysis are retained, including the counterfactual futility comparison. For the same seed, set of horizons, and other simulation settings, results agree with sim_horizon_paths() followed by apply_horizon_rules(). Event-time imputation, dropout interpretation, horizon-specific analysis settings, and the endpoint lock after a stop are described in sim_horizon_paths().

Examples

schedule <- data.frame(N = c(20, 40), horizon = c(12, 18))
result <- sim_horizon_trials(
  hazard_treatment = 0.04, hazard_control = 0.07,
  N_total = 60, endpoint_schedule = schedule, final_horizon = 18,
  lambda = 3, method = "bayes-bin", bin_method = "quadrature",
  alternative = "less", N_impute = 5, N_trials = 2, seed = 123
)
summarise_sims(result)
